rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that the prohibition cannot prove guardianship has legal effect here: if it did not show guardianship ineffective, it would not establish its effectiveness either.
rows.anchor: لو لم يدل على عدم تأثير الولاية في ذلك لم يدل على تأثيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is not demonstrably limited to guardians; it appears general, and the prohibition guides people to the benefits of allowing women to return to their former husbands.
rows.anchor: بل الظاهر أنه أعم منهم

rows.speaker: بعض القائلين
rows.claim: A reported reading addresses husbands, telling them not to conceal divorce and prolong the waiting period to stop remarriage; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects it because the text specifies their former husbands.
rows.anchor: وربما قيل إن الخطاب للأزواج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching the prescribed term means the waiting period has expired; before expiry, no guardian or anyone else could forbid the marriage in any case.
rows.anchor: فإن العدة لو لم تنقض لم يكن لأحد من الأولياء وغيرهم أن يمنع ذلك

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
ذلك يوعظ به من كان منكم يؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These two rulings uniquely invoke belief in God and the Last Day because monotheism calls people to unity and connection rather than separation.
rows.anchor: دين التوحيد يدعو إلى الاتحاد دون الافتراق

words: ذلك يوعظ به من كان منكم يؤمن بالله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discourse shifts between singular and plural: rulings address the whole community, while non-ruling clauses sometimes address the Prophet directly, preserving the speech's structure and his central role.
rows.anchor: والأصل في هذا الكلام خطاب المجموع أعني خطاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وأمته جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakāh here means wholesome, beneficial growth; the discussion of purity has been explained earlier.
rows.anchor: الزكاة هو النمو الصالح الطيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative refers either to not obstructing women's return to their husbands or to the return itself; both readings lead to the same point.
rows.anchor: عدم المنع عن رجوعهن إلى أزواجهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reunion repairs separation and strengthens the innate pull toward unity, allowing religious virtues to grow.
rows.anchor: رجوعا من الانثلام والانفصال إلى الالتئام والاتصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reunion cultivates women's chastity and modesty and protects their hearts from attachment to unrelated men if they are barred from marrying their former husbands.
rows.anchor: فيه تربية لملكة العفة والحياء فيهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam joins growth, purity, and knowledge, as shown by Qur'anic descriptions of the Messenger's teaching and of purification in ablution.
rows.anchor: والإسلام دين الزكاة والطهارة والعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People know only what God teaches; this does not conflict with God's limits being explained to people who know, since their knowledge comes through divine teaching.
rows.anchor: أي إلا ما يعلمكم كما قال تعالى ويعلمهم الكتاب والحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wālidāt means mothers who gave birth; it is narrower than al-ummahāt, just as al-wālid is narrower than al-ab and al-walad narrower than al-ibn.
rows.anchor: الوالدات هن الأمهات، وإنما عدل عن الأمهات إلى الوالدات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling concerns the birth mother, child, and father; calling the father al-mawlūd lahu hints that he must provide for the child's life and upbringing, including the nursing mother's clothing and support.
rows.anchor: والحكم في الآية مشروع في خصوص مورد الوالدة والولد والمولود له

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some exegetes say al-mawlūd lahu was chosen to show that children belong to fathers and are attributed to them, but the verse itself also calls them the mothers' children.
rows.anchor: ومن أعجب الكلام ما ذكر بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that children belong only to fathers overlooks the verse's opening and closing references to the mothers' children.
rows.anchor: وكأنه ذهل عن صدر الآية وذيلها حيث يقول تعالى أولادهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Maʾmūn's poem calls mothers vessels and says sons belong to fathers; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects this as insufficient support for God's wording.
rows.anchor: وإنما أمهات الناس أوعية مستودعات وللآباء أبناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many literary scholars confuse language, legislation, social convention, and natural fact, sometimes using linguistic evidence to claim a social rule or an ontological truth.
rows.anchor: وقد اختلط على كثير من علماء الأدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By nature a child derives from both parents; social attribution varies across peoples, and this verse reflects the convention that affiliates the child to the father.
rows.anchor: التكوين يلحقه بالوالدين معا لاستناده في وجوده إليهما معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Irḍāʿ is nursing: drawing milk from the breast by suckling.
rows.anchor: والإرضاع إفعال من الرضاعة والرضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ḥawl is a year, named for turning or passing around.
rows.anchor: والحول هو السنة سميت به لأنها تحول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The adjective complete removes ambiguity because a year or two years can be used loosely for a period that falls a few days short.
rows.anchor: وإنما وصف بالكمال لأن الحول والسنة لكونه ذا أجزاء كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divorced mother holds the right to custody and nursing, including whether to complete the two years; the father has no say unless both parents agree.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أن الحضانة والإرضاع حق للوالدة المطلقة موكول إلى اختيارها

words: وَعَلَى ٱلْمَوْلُودِ لَهُ رِزْقُهُنَّ وَكِسْوَتُهُنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mawlūd lahu means the father, who owes the nursing mothers customary maintenance and clothing, measured by their circumstances.
rows.anchor: المراد بالمولود له هو الوالد كما مر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general rule that no person is burdened beyond capacity grounds the customary scale and removes hardship from the family rulings.
rows.anchor: حكم عام آخر رافع للحرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because nursing and custody are the mother's rights, the father may not obstruct her custody, nursing, or access to the child; doing so would harm and burden her.
rows.anchor: فلا يحق للزوج أن يحول بين الوالدة وولدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother likewise may not harm the father by using the child to prevent visits or similar contact.
rows.anchor: نفي مضارة الزوجة للزوج بولده بأن تمنعه عن الرؤية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying his child instead of using a pronoun avoids an apparent contradiction: the child is biologically both parents' child but socially attributed to the father.
rows.anchor: أي إن الولد لهما معا تكوينا فهو ولده وولدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent reading transfers the father's maintenance and clothing obligation to his heir if he dies; other interpretations depart from the apparent text, while this reading agrees with Ahl al-Bayt reports.
rows.anchor: ظاهر الآية أن الذى جعل على الوالد من الكسوة والنفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiṣāl means weaning, and tashāwur means joint consultation.
rows.anchor: الفصال الفطام، والتشاور الاجتماع على المشورة

words: فَإِنْ أَرَادَا فِصَالًا عَن تَرَاضٍ مِّنْهُمَا وَتَشَاوُرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nursing and custody are rights the mother may waive, not duties fixed beyond change; parents may agree after consultation to wean early without blame.
rows.anchor: بل هو حق يمكنها أن تتركه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father may hire another nurse if the mother refuses or cannot nurse because of illness, lost milk, or another cause, provided he pays her due fairly and does not infringe her rights.
rows.anchor: من انقطاع لبن أو مرض ونحوه

words: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ
واتقوا الله واعلموا أن الله بكل شيء عليم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to fear God here concerns keeping outward actions sound, hence God is described as seeing deeds; the preceding passage also warns against harmful intent that may not yet show outwardly.
rows.anchor: أمر بالتقوى وان يكون هذا التقوى بإصلاح صورة هذه الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawaffā means to cause death; mutawaffā is its passive participle, meaning one who has died.
rows.anchor: يقال توفاه الله إذا أماته فهو متوفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadharūn means they leave, like yadaʿūn; neither verb has a past tense from its root.
rows.anchor: ويذرون مثل يدعون بمعنى يتركون ولا ماضي لهما من مادتهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word days is omitted after ten because the context makes it understood.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعشر الأيام حذفت لدلالة الكلام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching their term means the waiting period has ended; widows then have choice in their conduct, including remarriage, and relatives may not block what religious law permits.
rows.anchor: المراد ببلوغ الأجل انقضاء العدة

words: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيمَا فَعَلْنَ فِىٓ أَنفُسِهِنَّ بِٱلْمَعْرُوفِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Relatives cannot forbid widows from a lawful choice by customs rooted in ignorance, greed, or envy; no one may prohibit what religious law recognizes as good.
rows.anchor: وليس لقرابة الميت منعهن عن شيء من ذلك استنادا إلى بعض العادات

rows.speaker: بعض الأمم
rows.claim: Some peoples burned a living wife with her dead husband or buried her alive beside him.
rows.anchor: إحراق الزوجة الحية مع زوجها الميت أو إلحادها وإقبارها معه

rows.speaker: النصارى
rows.claim: Christians were said to forbid a widow from remarrying for the rest of her life.
rows.anchor: عدم جواز ازدواجها ما بقيت بعده إلى آخر عمرها كالنصارى

rows.speaker: العرب الجاهلي
rows.claim: Pre-Islamic Arabs required a widow to withdraw from men for a year after her husband's death.
rows.anchor: اعتزالها عن الرجال إلى سنة من حين الوفاة كالعرب الجاهلي

rows.speaker: بعض الملل الراقية
rows.claim: Some other communities imposed a period close to a year, such as nine months.
rows.anchor: أو ما يقرب من السنة كتسعة أشهر

rows.speaker: بعض الأقوام
rows.claim: Some communities believed a widow owed her deceased husband a period of abstention from remarriage but set no duration.
rows.anchor: حقا على الزوجة في الكف عن الازدواج حينا من غير تعيين للمدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These customs reflect the idea that marriage joins lives through affection and intimacy, so the surviving spouse should honor that bond; the duty weighs more on women because of modesty and chastity.
rows.anchor: وللحب حرمة يجب رعايتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam fixes the widow's waiting period at four months and ten days, approximately one third of a year.
rows.anchor: وقد عين الإسلام هذا التربص بما يقرب من ثلث سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's expertise suits the rulings on widow waiting and their subsequent right to marry: He distinguishes forbidden conduct from permitted choices.
rows.anchor: لما كان الكلام مشتملا على تشريع عدة الوفاة وعلى تشريع حق الازدواج لهن بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿrīḍ is indirect wording that turns toward a meaning for the listener to infer, as opposed to explicit declaration; praising one's companionship can hint at a marriage proposal.
rows.anchor: التعريض هو الميل بالكلام إلى جانب ليفهم المخاطب أمرا مقصودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike indirect allusion, a kināya has no intended meaning beyond the implied one; saying someone has much ash means that he is generous.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين التعريض والكناية أن للكلام الذي فيه التعريض معنى مقصودا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiṭba with kasra means speaking with a woman about marriage; khiṭba with ḍamma means addressing people, especially in preaching, with distinct terms for speakers in each usage.
rows.anchor: والخطبة بكسر الخاء من الخطب بمعنى التكلم والمراجعة في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iknān, from kinn, is concealment within oneself; kinn refers to cover provided by a physical object, garment, or house.
rows.anchor: والإكنان من الكن بالفتح بمعنى الستر

words: عَرَّضْتُم بِهِۦ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ ٱلنِّسَآءِ أَوْ أَكْنَنتُمْ فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse removes blame for indirectly proposing to a woman in her waiting period or keeping the desire to marry her in one's heart.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالآية نفي البأس عن التعريض في الخطبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering these women is natural to human temperament, so God does not prohibit an act required by innate disposition and creation; this exemplifies Islam's basis in fitra.
rows.anchor: ذكركم إياهن أمر مطبوع في طباعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm is a firm resolve in the heart that fixes an act without weakness unless the intention is canceled from its basis.
rows.anchor: العزم عقد القلب على الفعل وتثبيت الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUqda derives from tying, and the marriage bond is likened to a knot joining two threads into one connected whole.
rows.anchor: والعقدة من العقد بمعنى الشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The marriage bond is a rational convention grounded in intention and belief, like property and other social rights; its explanation continues with a reference to 2:213.
rows.anchor: أن سنخ هذه العقدة والعلقة أمر قائم بالنية والاعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses metaphor and metonymy in depicting the marriage bond as a knot resolved in the heart.
rows.anchor: ففي الآية استعارة وكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-kitāb means the prescribed ruling, namely the waiting period imposed by God on women observing it.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكتاب هو المكتوب أي المفروض من الحكم

words: وَلَا تَعْزِمُوا۟ عُقْدَةَ ٱلنِّكَاحِ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One must not conclude a marriage contract until the waiting period ends; this shows the prior permission concerns proposals and contracts with women in waiting periods, making al-nisāʾ contextually specific.
rows.anchor: ولا تجروا عقد النكاح حتى تنقضي عدتهن

words: وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِىٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning God's knowledge, forgiveness, and forbearance signals that proposals, indirect hints, and secret promises to women in waiting periods are perilous and not fully approved, though some are permitted.
rows.anchor: إيراد ما ذكر من صفاته تعالى في الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Touching is a euphemism for intercourse, and assigning a prescribed amount means naming the dower.
rows.anchor: المس كناية عن المواقعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divorce is valid even if the couple never had intercourse and even if no dower was specified.
rows.anchor: أن عدم مس الزوجة لا يمنع عن صحة الطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tamtiʿ is giving something for enjoyment; matāʿ and mutʿa name what is enjoyed, and matāʿan is an absolute object separated from its verb by an intervening phrase.
rows.anchor: التمتيع إعطاء ما يتمتع به

words: عَلَى ٱلْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وَعَلَى ٱلْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mūsiʿ is one with ample means, al-muqter one with narrow means, and al-qadr has the same meaning with either vowel on the dāl; awsaʿa is used intransitively after frequent object omission.
rows.anchor: والموسع اسم فاعل من أوسع إذا كان على سعة من المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A customary parting gift is due from a man who divorces a woman before intercourse when her dower was never specified; its amount follows the means of the wealthy or the poor.
rows.anchor: يجب عليكم أن تمتعوا المطلقات عن غير فرض فريضة متاعا بالمعروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surface wording makes beneficence appear to condition the ruling, which would imply recommendation because beneficence is not obligatory.
rows.anchor: كون الوصف أعني الإحسان دخيلا في الحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports from the Ahl al-Bayt make the gift obligatory; 2:229 already obligates good treatment by divorcers, who are the beneficent people named here.
rows.anchor: النصوص من طرق أهل البيت تفسر الحكم بالوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a man divorces before intercourse after specifying a dower, he owes half unless the woman waives it or the person holding the marriage bond waives it; that person can be her guardian or the husband, and she need not return half already received.
rows.anchor: فيجب عليكم تأدية نصف ما فرضتم من المهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgoing a right one legally owns is closer to piety and strengthens a person's ability to refrain from violating rights that are not theirs.
rows.anchor: والعفو على أي حال أقرب للتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faḍl is increase in virtues and praiseworthy qualities, unlike fuḍūl, which is said to mean blameworthy excess.
rows.anchor: الفضل هو الزيادة كالفضول غير أن الفضل هو الزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation encourages generosity in social life: spouses should forgive rights, act graciously, and ease matters for one another.
rows.anchor: الترغيب في الإحسان والفضل بالعفو عن الحقوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The note about God seeing all things has the same point as the corresponding statement at the end of the nursing passage.
rows.anchor: كالنكتة فيما مر في ذيل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥifẓ means guarding or keeping something; its use for preserving inward meanings is especially common.
rows.anchor: حفظ الشيء ضبطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-wusṭā is the feminine of al-awsaṭ and means the prayer situated in the middle; the Qur'an does not identify which prayer, leaving its interpretation to the Sunnah.
rows.anchor: والصلاة الوسطى هي الواقعة في وسطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-llāh expresses purpose; standing for an undertaking is figurative language for assuming and committing to it.
rows.anchor: القيام بأمر كناية عن تقلده والتلبس بفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qunūt is humble obedience; the phrase means undertaking God's obedience humbly and sincerely for His sake.
rows.anchor: والقنوت هو الخضوع بالطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional clause depends on an omitted condition: preserve prayer when you do not fear; under fear, perform it as far as possible, walking or riding. This is the prayer of fear.
rows.anchor: عطف الشرط على الجملة السابقة يدل على تقدير شرط محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is never dropped: when fear makes normal performance difficult, pray to the extent possible; when safety returns, the ordinary obligation resumes along with remembrance of God.
rows.anchor: بل إن لم تخافوا شيئا وأمكنت لكم وجبت عليكم

words: كَمَا عَلَّمَكُم مَّا لَمْ تَكُونُوا۟ تَعْلَمُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kāf expresses comparison, and the broad phrase what you did not know replaces a narrower reference to emphasize the breadth of God's teaching and favor.
rows.anchor: من قبيل وضع العام موضع الخاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After safety returns, remember God in a way resembling the prescribed prayer taught for secure conditions, within the broader body of religious rulings He taught.
rows.anchor: فاذكروا الله ذكرا يماثل ما علمكم من الصلاة المفروضة المكتوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fahm is the mind's reception of an external image; fiqh is settling that image into firm assent; dirāya penetrates further to grasp particulars and hidden qualities and is used to magnify a matter.
rows.anchor: والفهم نوع انفعال للذهن عن الخارج عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaqīn is cognition strengthened so it cannot be removed or weakened; fikr is movement through present information to derive unknowns that follow from it.
rows.anchor: واليقين هو اشتداد الإدراك الذهني بحيث لا يقبل الزوال والوهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Raʾy is assent reached through thought and deliberation, usually about practical duties rather than theoretical facts; basīra, iftāʾ, and qawl are related, with qawl used metaphorically for the belief implied by speech.
rows.anchor: والرأي هو التصديق الحاصل من الفكر والتروي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zaʿm describes assent as a mental image whether probable or absolutely certain; ʿilm is cognition that excludes its contrary.
rows.anchor: والزعم هو التصديق من حيث أنه صورة في الذهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥifẓ preserves a known image against change or disappearance, while ḥikma is knowledge made sound and exact.
rows.anchor: والحفظ ضبط الصورة المعلومة بحيث لا يتطرق إليه التغيير والزوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khibra is knowledge so manifest that the knower does not miss how a conclusion follows from its premises.
rows.anchor: والخبره هو ظهور الصورة العلمية بحيث لا يخفى على العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahāda is direct apprehension of the thing itself, through outward senses or inward awareness such as knowing, willing, loving, and hating.
rows.anchor: والشهادة هو نيل نفس الشيء وعينه إما بحس ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Terms tied to matter, motion, and change are not applied to God; ʿilm, ḥifẓ, ḥikma, khibra, and shahāda can be used because they imply no deficiency or loss.
rows.anchor: لا تستعمل في مورده تعالى غير الخمسة الأخيرة منها أعني العلم والحفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic descriptions of God as knowing, guarding, expert, wise, and witnessing illustrate the five attributes suitable to God.
rows.anchor: وربك على كل شيء حفيظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAql is perception joined to assent, grounded in the innate human capacity to recognize truth and falsehood in theory and good, evil, benefit, and harm in action.
rows.anchor: لفظ العقل على ما عرفت يطلق على الإدراك من حيث إن فيه عقد القلب بالتصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates humans able to perceive themselves, then equips them with outward senses and inward awareness of will, love, hate, hope, and fear; the mind orders these into theoretical and practical judgments.
rows.anchor: وبأخرى باطنة يدرك معاني روحية بها ترتبط نفسه مع الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When appetite or anger dominates other faculties, judgment leaves moderation for excess or deficiency and no longer operates according to sound innate nature.
rows.anchor: كالشهوة والغضب فأبطل حكم الباقي أو ضعفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person misled by false evidence resembles a judge who reaches an untrue verdict without intending falsehood: the form of judgment remains, but not its truth.
rows.anchor: كالقاضي الذي يقضي بمدارك أو شهادات كاذبة منحرفة محرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an reserves the name true intellect for reasoning that benefits religion and leads to sound knowledge and good action; merely worldly judgment is only figuratively called intellect.
rows.anchor: يعرف العقل بما ينتفع به الإنسان في دينه ويركب به هداه إلى حقائق المعارف
